transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees (Redwood): Maya Chen (AE), Carlos Rivera (SE)
Attendees (Customer): Samir Patel (CTO), Ruth Gomez (ML Eng), Owen Li (Infra), Priya Nair (Prod)

Summary:
Quick, practical walkthrough of Redwood Optimize sandbox focusing on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) and how BlueCrest can pick a precision profile that meets latency SLOs while protecting quality for their routing / manifest summarization use case. Plan to provision sandbox and run a paired benchmark next week.

Topics:
- baseline perf/quality measurements
- precision profiles and hybrid fallback rules
- KV cache effects on latency vs token cost
- rollout strategy and canarying in Dedicated/private contexts
- security, data retention, and audit logs

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, auto-generated, imperfect) ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Carlos will take us through the sandbox demo. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Samir: Good, thanks. Loud and clear. Appreciate you guys making time. We've got about 45 minutes, I think, right?
[00:13] Maya: Yup, ~45. We want this to be hands-on; we'll show the Optimize console, the quant profiles, and then walk through a sample int8 vs fp8 comparison we've run internally. We'll also leave time for questions and to align on next steps.
[00:26] Ruth: Quick ask — we care a lot about throughput during peak loads (our routing spikes around end of day). Latency P95 needs to be under 250ms for short prompts.
[00:35] Carlos: Great, thanks for that, Ruth. Keep that SLO in mind — we'll show latency numbers and what you can tune. Also want to call out that when we say FP8 you'll sometimes see it spelled E F P 8 in the console transcription — just a quirk.
[00:46] Owen: Also security question up front: can the sandbox live in our VPC or is it hosted only? We have to be sure about KMS and audit logs.
[00:53] Maya: Sandbox is hosted by default but we can deploy a Private trial into your VPC for the lab if needed; we'll share the security pack (SOC 2, SSO, KMS integration notes). We'll open a separate ticket for that.
[01:02] Carlos: Ok jumping in — I'm in the Optimize console. Opening the 'Precision Playbooks' tab. On the left you see profile presets: conservative, balanced, aggressive — those map to pre-tuned quantization layouts.
[01:18] Carlos: Real quick caveat: some of the auto metrics are approximate when using our streaming mock in the sandbox — for exact numbers we recommend running the bench harness that we'll provision.
[01:30] [01:30] Carlos: So here's an INT8 profile test we did on a 70B opt-style model: throughput improved ~2.3x vs fp32, latency P95 dropped by 40-50ms for short prompts, and token cost was down significantly. But you do see a small degradation in rare edge-case completions — that's the usual tradeoff.
[01:55] Ruth: How are you measuring degradation? Is that BLEU or embedding distance or human eval?
[02:02] Carlos: We use a combo: embedding similarity on a holdout set + a lightweight hallucination check + spot human evals for critical prompts. In the console we surface a quality delta heatmap that shows percent of responses below an embedding similarity threshold (we call it "fidelity lane").
[02:20] Maya: For BlueCrest you'll want to pick a threshold tied to your manifest summarization quality target. If a candidate model crosses that threshold, the rollout can automatically fall back to a higher-precision profile.
[02:33] Samir: So are fallbacks automatic? We can't tolerate periods where model outputs silently degrade.
[02:38] Carlos: Yes, fallback rules are policy-driven. You can set conditions like "if average embedding similarity < 0.88 for 5m, switch to balanced FP8 profile" or "if P95 latency > 300ms, switch to INT8-low-batch and route higher SLAs to Dedicated nodes". There was a tiny transcription glitch earlier — we call it FP8, F-P-8 — but the policies are flexible.
[03:04] Priya: Can policies be tested in a canary before global rollout?
[03:08] Carlos: Absolutely. We have canary gates, A/B splits, and you can pin traffic percentages. In the console demo in a sec you'll see the rollout widget which lets you run a 5% canary for 2 hours and watch the fidelity/latency panels.
[03:20] [03:20] Carlos: Switching to the 'Bench Lab' dashboard — here's a sample report we ran for BlueCrest-like workload. Column on the left shows INT8 / FP8 / HYBRID. The latency column — look at P50/P95/P99. The quality column shows embedding delta and a small human-verified error rate.
[03:36] Carlos: Note: hybrid means we run a mixed precision path — most tokens in INT8, critical layers in FP8 — yields a middle ground. We can generate profiles programmatically via the Optimize API too.
[03:49] Ruth: Does the KV cache behavior change between INT8 and FP8? We've seen cache thrash cause spikes in p95.
[03:55] Carlos: Good question. KV cache semantics are the same, but quantization impacts memory usage and cache hit patterns. In aggressive INT8 you might pack cache differently, which can increase cold-start latency on longer contexts. Optimize will surface cache hit rates and advise batch sizes.
[04:14] Owen: For our infra team — if we run this on Dedicated, will the autoscaler respect the precision profiles? Meaning if we choose an INT8 profile, do we get different instance sizes?
[04:23] Carlos: Autoscaling has knobs per-profile. For Dedicated pools you can map profiles to GPU types and target concurrency. For example, INT8 can run on smaller cards or double concurrency per GPU; we show recommended GPU SKU and batch size.
[04:36] Samir: Pricing — how is cost modeled between INT8 and FP8? Is it just per-token or do you factor in throughput gains?
[04:43] Maya: Pricing is usage-based. Optimize will show a cost-per-inference estimate factoring in token count, batch efficiency, and instance utilization. The sheet Carlos will share has a modeled cost-per-1M tokens for each profile.
[04:57] [04:57] Carlos: I'm going to do a live quick demo — I'll upload three small prompt families and run a 10-minute sweep. Keep in mind sandbox will be throttled but it's representative.
[05:08] Carlos: Uploading prompt set now... (pause) Ok starting sweep — INT8, FP8, hybrid. You'll see live charts for latency and embedding delta on the right.
[06:10] [06:10] Carlos: Sweep started — early numbers coming in: INT8 P95 ~ 210ms, FP8 P95 ~ 265ms, hybrid P95 ~ 230ms for these short prompts. Embedding delta is 0.02 for INT8 vs baseline and 0.008 for FP8. For your target 250ms P95, INT8 looks good but we need to check the quality tail.
[06:38] Ruth: That embedding delta number — what threshold equates to 'bad' for us? We need a rule we can rely on.
[06:44] Carlos: Usually customers pick 0.03 as an upper tolerance for creative tasks, 0.015 for deterministic summarization. For manifests I'd suggest 0.012. If it crosses that, we trigger fallback.
[06:59] Samir: How noisy are these numbers across different prompt lengths? Our prompts range 20-500 tokens.
[07:06] Carlos: Short prompts favor INT8 latency wins. Long context can amplify quantization artifacts and cold KV cache effects. We recommend partitioning by prompt length in the bench harness and creating per-segment profiles — that's a common pattern we demoed with a retail client.
[07:22] Priya: Could we route short/high-priority requests to INT8 and long/complex ones to FP8 automatically? We want rule-based routing in front of the API.
[07:29] Carlos: Yes — Smart routing + Optimize profiles can be combined: request inspector routes based on metadata (prompt length, customer tier, etc.) to a profile. On the console you can define matchers like regex or size buckets.
[07:42] Maya: We actually have a short example rule in the docs — we'll link it.
[07:46] Owen: About stability — have you seen regressions where a profile that looked fine in lab later failed in prod? How do we monitor?
[07:53] Carlos: We tie quality monitoring to specific prompt sets and have regression alerts. If fidelity drops we open a regression incident and can auto roll back to the last known-good profile. Also we've built an "explain" view showing which layers or tokens triggered degradations so our SEs can triage faster.
[08:12] Samir: Can the rollback be instantaneous? We cannot have 30 minutes with bad outputs.
[08:18] Carlos: It can be fast — you set the policy: immediate switch vs gradual. We usually recommend an immediate fallback to a pinned variant for critical workloads.
[08:27] [08:27] Ruth: I noticed you mentioned cost modeling — for a sustained peak of 3k rps what would you expect for compute? This is hypothetical but helps scoping Dedicated.
[08:35] Carlos: High-level: INT8 lets you pack ~2-2.5x throughput per GPU vs FP32; FP8 sits between INT8 and float32, so budgeting depends on model size and batch. We'll run a synthetic 3k RPS bench in the lab and give SKU recommendations for Dedicated.
[08:49] Maya: We'll also include a recommended reserved capacity proposal in the follow-up so you can compare costs.
[08:54] Samir: Security — there's an audit trail requirement from procurement: can we get per-request logs with redaction? And is SSO enforced for the sandbox?
[09:03] Maya: Yes on both counts. Sandbox supports SSO via SAML, and audit logs are available. We can redact PII fields at ingest or in post-processing; we support KMS-based key management for private deployments.
[09:15] [09:15] Carlos: Ok, fast-forward — results just finished for the sweep. I'm going to open the bench report link (I'll paste the internal sheet after the call). Here's a small table:
- INT8: cost est $0.45/1k tokens, P95 210ms, embedding delta 0.02, human-error 0.6%
- FP8: cost est $0.62/1k tokens, P95 265ms, embedding delta 0.008, human-error 0.2%
- Hybrid: cost est $0.53/1k tokens, P95 230ms, embedding delta 0.01
[09:47] Ruth: Those numbers look promising. That human-error metric — how reliable is it? We need to know whether 0.6% means actual customer visible issues.
[09:56] Carlos: The human-error is sampled on edge cases. 0.6% indicates among sampled prompts a small rate of quality regressions; we recommend increasing human vetting on that set or elevating the fallback threshold until the rate is acceptable.
[10:07] Samir: Could we do partial decoding or confidence triggers? If the model is uncertain, escalate to a higher precision in real time? That could reduce cost while protecting critical outputs.
[10:16] Carlos: Yes, we have a confidence scoring hook — when below threshold, route to FP8/FP32 for re-generation or attach a caution flag. The console has a 'confidence gate' you can enable per-route.
[10:29] Priya: How do we integrate this with our existing API gateway? Do we need to change SDKs?
[10:35] Maya: No major SDK change — Optimize exposes a routing header and SDK flag; your gateway can set the profile header based on request metadata. We'll share example code for Node/Python.
[10:44] Owen: For Private deployment, any difference in how fallback happens? If we host on-prem, do we still get automatic cloud fallback?
[10:51] Carlos: For Private you choose fallback strategy. You can have a hybrid where Private first, then Dedicated/reactive to cloud for overflow. Automatic cloud fallback requires network connectivity; if air-gapped, fallback is local profile swap.
[11:05] [11:05] Ruth: Could you show the rollout widget demo? I want to see the canary metrics live.
[11:09] Carlos: Sure — opening the rollout view. You set traffic percent, duration, and fidelity thresholds. I'm starting a 10% canary for 1 hour on the INT8 profile. Charts populate — you'll see fidelity and latency on separate series.
[11:29] Carlos: See that small uptick in embedding delta at minute 2? You can click into the example prompts and see which tokens changed. That's the 'explain' view.
[11:40] Samir: Pretty neat. That explain view will be critical for us to justify rolling to product teams.
[11:45] Maya: Quick note on naming — we can label profiles for accounting (e.g., profile-INT8-fast, profile-FP8-fidelity) so your billing and product tags map cleanly.
[11:54] Ruth: Regarding the bench harness — will your Carlos run it on an exact model architecture we run in prod? We use a custom fine-tuned LLaMA variant.
[12:03] Carlos: We can run on a compatible model family; if you want us to test your exact fine-tuned weights, we'd need a short security agreement to ingest them into the sandbox or do the bench on-prem. We can walk that process with security.
[12:18] Samir: Let's talk about timeline: if we get the sandbox next week and bench results, how long to go to pilot? We want a pilot in two months if possible.
[12:26] Maya: Pilot in 6-8 weeks is reasonable: week 0 sandbox + bench, week 2 lab deep-dive, week 4 pilot config + canary, week 6 pilot ramp. We'll send a suggested timeline.
[12:37] [12:37] Ruth: One practical question — how do model updates affect precision profiles? If we upgrade the model, do we need to re-run all sensitivity tests?
[12:44] Carlos: Yes, model changes can shift quant sensitivity. Optimize keeps versioned profiles tied to model commits. You can pin a profile to a model version and then run a quick re-sweep on new versions; the console will warn if a profile hasn't been validated for the new model.
[12:58] Owen: If we do Dedicated, do you support bring-your-own-GPU (we have existing p4d nodes) or must we buy through Redwood?
[13:06] Maya: We support hybrid: you can bring certain SKUs and we can run our runtime there; otherwise we can recommend a reserved pool. We'll include options in the follow-up.
[13:15] Samir: Any gotchas for quantization and legal — e.g., do we risk changing output semantics that could impact regulatory compliance? We operate in regulated logistics data.
[13:25] Carlos: This is why regression tests and explainability are important. For regulated outputs we recommend conservative profiles with stricter thresholds and more robust human-in-the-loop checks. We'll attach a compliance playbook.
[13:39] [13:39] Maya: Ok we're approaching the final 30 minutes, want to open floor for any final technical questions before we wrap to next steps.
[13:47] Ruth: Could you send the bench spreadsheet and a sample config for the canary? Also a sample policy for fallback thresholds?
[13:53] Maya: Yes — action item. Carlos will run the sweep and share the sheet; I'll share the sandbox invite and security pack.
[13:59] Samir: We'll also send our top-200 prompts and a short doc on SLOs and what's considered a failure.
[14:05] Priya: One last: the cost model — can you run a cost-sensitivity for different traffic shapes? We have big spikes and longer tails.
[14:11] Carlos: Yep we have a sensitivity tool — we'll include in the bench output.
[14:16] [14:16] Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Maya provisions sandbox; Carlos runs detailed int8/fp8/hybrid bench and posts sheet; BlueCrest uploads prompts; schedule 2-hour lab for the week of 1/25.
[14:28] Maya: Any blockers?
[14:29] Samir: No blockers from our side. Thanks, this was helpful.
[14:32] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and links within 24 hours.

End of transcript (auto-generated). Some speaker labels may be approximate and transcription contains occasional word errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "EFP8" for FP8). Links mentioned: bench spreadsheet (internal link to be shared), security pack (SOC2, SSO, KMS docs).
